titleStmt.title: Shiji 史记 · 秦王政元年: notes

div.interp: 年十三岁: King Zhuangxiang died in 247 BC; Zheng's first year as king is this year, 246 BC.
二周: the Western and Eastern Zhou domains, extinguished in 256 and 249 BC (see those years).
舍人: the Jijie cites Wen Ying: the title of a petty officer in charge of the stables; or, retainers in attendance are called sheren.

王齮: the Jijie cites Xu Guang, one text 齕. The Suoyin: Meng Ao was a man of Qi, father of Meng Wu and grandfather of Meng Tian; Wang Yi is Wang He 王齕, who in King Zhao's forty-ninth year replaced the Grand Master Ling in attacking Zhao. The Zhengyi gives the reading of 齮 as yi (魚綺反); Liu Bozhuang reads it qi.

麃公: the Jijie cites Ying Shao, Biao is a Qin town; the Suoyin: probably the lord of the town of Biao, his surname and name lost to history; the Zhengyi: 麃 read biao (彼苗反), probably a County town of Qin, and a Grand Master is called 公 as in the Chu system.
246 BC. The Table (§2) and the Hereditary House of Zhao (§3) record the taking of Jinyang.
